precepts.text: She did not know that I gave her corn, and wine, and oil, and multiplied her silver and gold, which they prepared for Baal. The Lord clothed and fed us and we turned around and served the devil with it.
precepts.point: The children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, served Baalim, and forsook the Lord God of their fathers which brought them out of Egypt. They served Baal and Ashtaroth. That stubbornness is our history and why we are in captivity.
precepts.why:
Judges says Israel “served Baalim” and “forsook the Lord God of their fathers, which brought them out of the land of Egypt”. Hosea shows how ungrateful that was: “For she did not know that I gave her corn, and wine, and oil, and multiplied her silver and gold, which they prepared for Baal.”

That is what the Lord did for Israel. He clothed us, gave us land, gave us food and possessions, all of that. And we turned around and prepared it for Baal; we started serving the devil with what God gave us. Baal, Baalim, it is the same thing: the Canaanite god of fertility, storms, thunder and lightning, worshipped in horrible ways, whose name means lord or master. He sounds like Thor. Baal and Ashtaroth have taken on so many names over the ages, which is why we rarely hear of them, but the worship is coming back to light.

Even now it goes on. Just days before this class, thousands of Afro-Brazilians gathered on a Rio beach to offer gifts to a sea goddess, Yemanja, revered in the Yoruba religion as the mother of all orishas and humanity. Brazil is the tribe of Asher. It is the same deity all throughout: “the women knead their dough, to make cakes to the queen of heaven”. Ashtaroth, the queen of heaven, Yemanja, whatever the name. Our people carried that witchcraft with them and kept doing it, even in Africa.

That's our history, and that is why we are in captivity today, catching hell. The Lord clothed us and named us, yet even in 2026 our people are still worshipping the devil, and we wonder why America goes down there stealing presidents, starving people out and destabilizing countries.

precepts.text: I will sow her unto me in the earth, and I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy, and I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art my God.
precepts.point: Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God, which had not obtained mercy but now have obtained mercy. Peter is quoting Hosea 2:23 about the northern kingdom.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
“And the earth shall hear the corn, and the wine, and the oil; and they shall hear Jezreel.” Jezreel is the seed of Israel. This is chapter 2 of the same context as Hosea 1:10-11, read earlier, where God gathers them together again and they appoint themselves one head.

“And I will sow her unto me in the earth”: I will bring her, adopt her back unto me in the earth. Then, “and I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy; and I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art my God.” Which were not my people, or not a people. That promise was made to the northern kingdom, in Isaiah 7 and 8 and in Hosea 1.

Now go back to Peter. He is writing to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia and the rest, the elect according to the foreknowledge of God, and he says “Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.” Sound familiar? Peter is quoting Hosea. When Christ dies he redeems them back into being his people and gathers them together in one.

The builders who stumbled were appointed to it: by rejecting Christ they had him killed, and by his being killed the northern kingdom was granted a chance to repent and be redeemed back into the fold. Israelites that are not studying never see this. How could you find that out if you don't know your history?

precepts.text: Israel played the harlot with many lovers, yet the Most High still calls her to return again to him.
precepts.point: He will not have mercy upon her children, for they be children of whoredoms, and their mother has played the harlot, saying she will go after her lovers that give her bread, water, wool, flax, oil, and drink. This is Israel following the other nations that ruled over them.
precepts.why:
Israel’s mother “hath played the harlot”, saying “I will go after my lovers, that give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, mine oil and my drink.” This is Israel following the other nations that ruled over them. Jeremiah says the same: “thou hast played the harlot with many lovers”.

Yet notice what follows. “If a man put away his wife, and she go from him, and become another man’s, shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted?” Even so, “yet return again to me, saith the Lord.” Israel played the harlot with many lovers, and the Most High still calls her to return again to him.

precepts.text: For all the causes whereby backsliding Israel committed adultery, he put her away and gave her a bill of divorcement, and her treacherous sister Judah followed and played the harlot also.
precepts.point: He will not have mercy upon her children, for they be children of whoredoms, and their mother has played the harlot, saying she will go after her lovers that give her bread, water, wool, flax, oil, and drink. This is Israel following the other nations that ruled over them.
precepts.why:
“For their mother hath played the harlot: she that conceived them hath done shamefully”. Jeremiah shows the Most High’s answer to that harlotry: “for all the causes whereby backsliding Israel committed adultery I had put her away, and given her a bill of divorce”. He put Israel away for going after her lovers, the other nations that ruled over them.

And it did not stop there: “yet her treacherous sister Judah feared not, but went and played the harlot also.” Judah followed Israel and played the harlot too.

precepts.text: The Most High keeps referring to Israel as her because he has likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman, a bride.
precepts.point: He will sow her unto himself in the earth, have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy, and say to them which were not his people, Thou art my people, and they shall say, Thou art my God. This is what is going on now as all people are repenting.
precepts.why:
“I will sow her unto me in the earth; and I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy”. The Most High keeps referring to Israel as her. “I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman.” Israel is his bride, a comely and delicate woman, and that is why she is her.

He will say “to them which were not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art my God.” This is what is going on now as all people are repenting.

precepts.text: He will say to them which were not his people, "Thou art my people," and they shall say, "Thou art my God."
precepts.point: The restoration is two sticks made one nation. Ephraim, once "not a people," is called back and named the sons of the living God, having obtained mercy that they had not obtained, so the Gentiles being brought in are the outcasts of Israel that Christ came to be a light to.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy; and I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art my God.”

The house of Israel was told “I will no more have mercy”, and here the Most High has mercy on her that had not obtained mercy. Ephraim, who was not his people, is called his people again. That is who God showed Peter not to call common or unclean.

points: Say unto your brethren Ammi, my people, and to your sisters Ruhamah, that have obtained mercy.
Plead with your mother, plead, for she is not my wife, neither am I her husband; let her put away her whoredoms and her adulteries from between her breasts.
Lest he strip her naked and set her as in the day she was born, make her a wilderness, set her like a dry land, and slay her with thirst.

He will not have mercy upon her children, for they be children of whoredoms, and their mother has played the harlot, saying she will go after her lovers that give her bread, water, wool, flax, oil, and drink. This is Israel following the other nations that ruled over them.
Therefore he will hedge up her way with thorns and make a wall, that she shall not find her paths; she shall follow her lovers but not overtake them, and seek them but not find them.

Then she says she will go and return to her first husband, for then it was better with her than now, for she did not know that he gave her the corn, the wine, and the oil, and multiplied her silver and gold, which they prepared for Baal while she went to idolatry.

Therefore he will return and take away his corn and his wine in their season, and recover his wool and his flax given to cover her nakedness. Even though it came through the nations, he allowed them to give it to her and made sure they nurtured her, so she was not left out in the cold even while oppressed.
Now he will discover her lewdness in the sight of her lovers, and none shall deliver her out of his hand; when he gets ready to chastise, nobody is going to stop it.
He will cause all her mirth to cease, her feast days, her new moons, her sabbaths, and all her solemn feasts, stripping the high holy days from her.

He will destroy her vines and her fig trees, whereof she said these are my rewards that my lovers have given me, and make them a forest for the beasts to eat. Like today, all people think America is blessing them, but it is the Most High giving them whatever little they have.
He will visit upon her the days of Baalim, wherein she burned incense, decked herself with earrings and jewels, went after her lovers, and forgot him.
Therefore he will allure her, bring her into the wilderness, and speak comfortably unto her.
He will give her her vineyards from thence, and the valley of Achor for a door of hope, and she shall sing there as in the days of her youth, as in the day she came up out of the land of Egypt.
At that day she shall call him Ishi, my husband, and no more Baali, my lord.
He will take away the names of Baalim out of her mouth, and they shall no more be remembered by their name.

In that day he will make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field, the fowls of heaven, and the creeping things of the ground, and break the bow and the sword and the battle out of the earth, and make them to lie down safely.

He will betroth her unto himself forever, in righteousness, in judgment, in lovingkindness, and in mercies, and in faithfulness, and she shall know the Lord. This is where the Most High accepts us again, serving one God and being faithful to that one God.
In that day he will hear the heavens, and they shall hear the earth, and the earth shall hear the corn and the wine and the oil, and they shall hear Jezreel.

He will sow her unto himself in the earth, have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy, and say to them which were not his people, Thou art my people, and they shall say, Thou art my God. This is what is going on now as all people are repenting.
